title: One-column extension of a prescribed Cartan–Eilenberg boundary comparison
statement: Let $A,B$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian], $F:A\to B$ exact and additive, $K,L$ complexes indexed by $\mathbf Z$, and $u:F(K)\to L$ a chain map. Let $I,J$ be bicomplexes with horizontal index $\mathbf Z$ and resolution index $\mathbf N$ [def-sp-double-complex-total], augmented by $e_I:K[0]\to I$ and $e_J:L[0]\to J$. Fix $p\in\mathbf Z$ and $q=p+1$. Assume the augmented original-object, cycle, boundary and homology columns in degree $p$, and the outgoing boundary column $\operatorname{Im}(d^{q-1,q})$, are quasi-isomorphisms. Assume the corresponding terms of $J$ are injective [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Put $\varepsilon_I^r=\mathrm{singleObjXSelf}^{-1}\circ(e_I^r)^0$ and define $\varepsilon_J^r$ similarly, and $G=F$ applied to resolution complexes. Given a chain map $b:G(\operatorname{Im}(d_I^{p-1,p}))\to\operatorname{Im}(d_J^{p-1,p})$ with $b^0 F(\operatorname{factorThruImage}(d_I^{p-1,p})^0\varepsilon_I^{p-1})=\operatorname{factorThruImage}(d_J^{p-1,p})^0\varepsilon_J^{p-1}u^{p-1}$, there exist chain maps $x:G(I^p)\to J^p$ and $c:G(\operatorname{Im}(d_I^{q-1,q}))\to\operatorname{Im}(d_J^{q-1,q})$ such that $x^0F(\varepsilon_I^p)=\varepsilon_J^pu^p$, $c$ obeys the same boundary augmentation equation at $q$, $xG(\operatorname{image.\iota}(d_I^{p-1,p}))=\operatorname{image.\iota}(d_J^{p-1,p})b$, and $cG(\operatorname{factorThruImage}(d_I^{q-1,q}))=\operatorname{factorThruImage}(d_J^{q-1,q})x$, identifying columns $p=q-1$ with the displayed eqToHom maps. No comparisons in other original-object columns or boundedness hypotheses are asserted.

proof.text: In degrees $p$ and $q=p+1$, form the two short exact sequences of resolution complexes $0\to B^p\to Z^p\to H^p\to0$ and $0\to Z^p\to I^p\to B^q\to0$ and the corresponding sequences for $J$. Their augmentations come from the single bicomplex augmentations. Exactness of $F$ preserves the sequences and augmented quasi-isomorphisms. The hypothesis on the incoming boundary map $b$, stated after precomposing with $K^{p-1}\to B^p(K)$, is the genuine boundary augmentation square because this map is epic and remains epic under $F$. Evaluation in a resolution degree is exact; hence the row sequences are degreewise short exact. All needed target columns are injective resolutions by the explicitly local quasi-isomorphism and termwise injectivity assumptions.

Lift the homology augmentation through the monomorphic quasi-isomorphism from $F(H^p(K))[0]$ into the source homology resolution, into the termwise injective target homology resolution, using [lem-weil-pbc-lift-along-injective-quasi-iso] (Tag 013P(2)). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-horseshoe-morphism-lift-exact-source] to the boundary/cycle/homology sequences with this homology map and the prescribed boundary map $b$. This produces an augmented cycle comparison commuting with both endpoint inclusions.

Independently lift the outgoing boundary augmentation to the injective outgoing boundary column of $J$ by [lem-weil-pbc-lift-along-injective-quasi-iso], obtaining $c$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-horseshoe-morphism-lift-exact-source] to the cycle/object/outgoing-boundary short exact sequences, prescribing the cycle map of the previous step and this same map $c$. Its middle map $x$ has the required object augmentation and outgoing factorThruImage equation.

Compose the incoming endpoint equation of the object horseshoe with the boundary-to-cycle inclusion and use the incoming endpoint equation of the cycle horseshoe to get the equation for image.ι. Retain the outgoing augmentation square of $c$. These are exactly the four displayed conclusions. Since $q-1=p$, the displayed eqToHom maps merely identify the same original-object column with that indexed by $q-1$. No induction or assembly of all original-object columns occurs in this lemma.
